title: Self-trading competitive scorecard
scope: ARX self-trading (automated agent trading) vs MetaTrader 5, TradingView, QuantConnect LEAN, NinjaTrader, cTrader Automate, Interactive Brokers TWS API, Freqtrade.
policy: No aggregate or percentage score. Competitor facts only from cited official documentation; anything not retrieved is marked unverified. ARX 'ahead' is limited to documented semantics and never implies broker-verified superiority.

status_values.ahead: ARX's documented and offline-tested behaviour exceeds what the cited competitor documentation describes; not broker-verified.
status_values.parity-claimed-unverified: ARX implements a comparable control, but evidence is offline only or the comparison is not measured.
status_values.behind: Competitors document a capability that ARX lacks or implements only partially.
status_values.not measured: No measurement exists on ARX and/or no comparable competitor figure was found.

evidence_levels_note: offline-tested = repository tests with fixtures/disposable PostgreSQL/extracted-handler harness; broker-verified = observed on a real MT5 demo or live account. No self-trading agent row is broker-verified. The repository records one controlled manual LIVE micro-test (artifacts/api-server/src/scripts/liveMicroTestFinalize.ts) on a non-agent path; it was not re-verified here.

rows.capability: Pre-submission broker check of margin and request validity

competitors.approach: OrderCheck() validates a request and returns projected balance, equity, margin, free margin and margin level plus a return code before OrderSend(); a true result is not a promise of execution.
TWS order precautions warn/confirm before transmission; API users can bypass them individually (bypassOrderPrecautions etc.).

rows.arx_current_state: Server-side broker symbol guard (min/max volume, volume step, freeze distance, SL/TP proximity) runs in the live pipeline preflight; the EA runs its own RunPreflight before CTrade. No OrderCheck() call exists in any EA, so projected margin/free margin is never checked at the terminal.
rows.arx_evidence_level: offline-tested (server guard); EA preflight compiled only in C++ harness; broker-unverified
rows.acceptance_criterion: Every automated entry runs OrderCheck() (or equivalent margin projection) immediately before submission; a failing check refuses with the broker retcode recorded; extracted-handler tests cover insufficient margin, invalid volume, invalid stops and auto-trading disabled (10027).

rows.capability: Maximum slippage (price deviation) cap on market orders

competitors.approach: MqlTradeRequest.deviation sets the maximum deviation in points; it is a required field only for Request and Instant execution modes, not Market/Exchange execution.
Market orders are sent with optional parameters via ExecuteMarketOrder; the trading-operations page does not name a slippage parameter (market-range semantics unverified).

rows.arx_current_state: v131 live poll applies SetDeviationInPoints with a compile-time ceiling of 20 points that the server can only tighten; v154 uses an input MaxSlippagePoints (default 30). Because deviation is ignored on market-execution symbols, ARX has no post-fill slippage check.
rows.acceptance_criterion: (a) Deviation cap applied on every automated entry; (b) for market-execution symbols, measured |fill price - requested price| is recorded per fill and fills beyond the cap raise an execution-quality event; (c) demo-broker test shows both behaviours.
rows.notes: Parity only for request/instant execution symbols; market-execution coverage is missing.

rows.capability: Spread re-check between decision and dispatch

competitors.approach: Precautions flag limit orders too far from the market by percentage or number of ticks.
Backtests can use fixed, live-symbol or random spread, so spread sensitivity can be evaluated before deployment.

rows.arx_current_state: Decision engine still passes maxSpreadPoints: null; the agent executor has no spread check (audit gap G1 remains open). The EA deviation cap is the only backstop.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Executor refuses with SPREAD_TOO_WIDE when observed live spread (with source and timestamp) exceeds the agent limit, and refuses when spread is unobservable; tests cover wide, stale and missing quotes.

rows.capability: Truthful fill result: executed volume, price, deal ID and partial fills

competitors.approach: MqlTradeResult carries retcode, deal, order, broker-confirmed volume and price, request_id and retcode_external; retcode 10009 is DONE and 10010 DONE_PARTIAL.
Order tickets update automatically; PARTIALLY_FILLED is a distinct status and an order is closed only when filled, canceled or invalid.
TradeResult exposes IsSuccessful, Error, Position and PendingOrder.

rows.arx_current_state: Server lifecycle refuses to treat partial or unknown outcomes as full fills. Terminal side is weaker: v131 reports LIVE_FILLED from the CTrade boolean and sends the requested lot as executedVolume for entries; v154 maps every non-10009 retcode, including 10010 DONE_PARTIAL, to REJECTED and its result payload omits ResultVolume/ResultPrice (deal ID only inside a text comment).
rows.arx_evidence_level: server rules offline-tested; terminal behaviour source-reviewed; broker-unverified
rows.acceptance_criterion: EA maps 10009/10010/10008/other retcodes to FILLED/PARTIAL/PLACED/REJECTED-or-UNKNOWN; results carry ResultVolume, ResultPrice, ResultDeal, position identifier and request time; server never records executed volume it did not receive; extracted-handler test matrix covers every retcode in the MQL5 table; demo test reproduces a partial or rejected fill.
rows.notes: Highest-risk finding: a partial fill reported as REJECTED can leave real exposure that ARX believes does not exist.

rows.capability: Execution-quality measurement (slippage, latency, live vs simulation)

competitors.approach: Runs an out-of-sample backtest in parallel with each live deployment and overlays live and backtest equity and fills.
Tester can model zero, fixed or random execution delay (0-8 s 90% of the time, 9-18 s otherwise).

rows.arx_current_state: No per-fill slippage or latency record exists for self-trade executions. missionExecutionQuality is a block/downgrade pre-check for Profit Mission and is not imported by the self-trade executor.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Per automated fill: requested price, fill price, signed slippage in points and account currency, decision→claim→pickup→broker-result timestamps; median/p95/p99 reported per symbol and broker; dashboard and weekly report; live-vs-simulation divergence computed for each agent.

rows.capability: Asynchronous broker events processed without ordering assumptions

competitors.approach: OnTradeTransaction arrival order is not guaranteed and the queue holds 1024 elements; one request can produce several transactions.
ExecuteMarketOrderAsync returns a TradeOperation with IsExecuting and an optional completion callback.

rows.arx_current_state: Settlement treats receipt sequence as server observation order, not broker order; identical retries are idempotent and contradictions are retained as evidence. The EA does not use OnTradeTransaction for automated results.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Fault tests deliver duplicated, reordered and dropped result events and show no double application, no lost exposure and HELD state for contradictions; demo test confirms with real terminal events.

rows.capability: Risk-based lot sizing from stop distance, contract size and account-currency conversion

competitors.approach: stake_amount per trade (fixed or 'unlimited') and tradable_balance_ratio (default 0.99) cap the capital used.
ATM strategies size stop and target orders to the position and resize them when the position is added to.
Risk models receive and adjust PortfolioTarget objects from portfolio construction, chained in order.

rows.arx_current_state: computeRiskAwareLot divides an account-currency risk budget by stop distance × contract size × quote→account FX, rounds down to lot step, and refuses with NO_CONTRACT_SPEC or NO_QUOTE_FX rather than guessing. AACI may reduce size; quota regimes apply multipliers.
rows.acceptance_criterion: For each supported symbol class, sized lot × stop distance × value-per-lot equals the risk budget within one lot step (never above); verified against broker contract specs on a demo account for at least FX majors, JPY crosses, metals and indices.
rows.notes: Design refuses unknown contract specs, which the cited competitor docs do not describe; superiority is not claimed without broker verification.

competitors.approach: OrderCheck returns projected margin, free margin and margin level.
Total Value Limit and Algorithm Total Value Limit (default 10× the manual limit, per archived guide) gate order notional.

rows.arx_current_state: Agent admission reserves position count and daily attempt headroom, not cash margin or portfolio VaR. The shared Risk Governor applies leverage ceilings (gross notional/equity 30, single symbol 15).
rows.acceptance_criterion: Agent admission includes pending + open margin from broker-reported margin requirements; refusals when projected free margin < configured floor; test with concurrent agents sharing one account.

competitors.approach: TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_VOLUME (10034) and invalid-volume refusals come from the trade server.

rows.arx_current_state: Sizer rounds down to lot step; pre-trade broker guard refuses VOLUME_OFF_STEP and out-of-range volumes; EA preflight rechecks.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Zero broker volume rejections across a demo run covering every enabled symbol; any 10014/10034 rejection is recorded with symbol specs.

rows.capability: Daily loss limit with automatic flatten

competitors.approach: Account Daily Loss Limit (NinjaTrader Brokerage accounts): on breach working orders are cancelled, positions liquidated and later orders rejected for the session; staff state no mobile/email notification is sent.
dailyLossAutoLiq / dailyLossPercentageAutoLiq trigger liquidation, unlock at next open; alert and liquidate-only thresholds below.
MaxDrawdown protection locks trading for a duration after drawdown over a lookback exceeds max_allowed_drawdown; equity mode recommended.
A Maximum Portfolio Drawdown risk model exists (parameters not retrievable in this research).

rows.arx_current_state: Phase B gate DAILY_LOSS_LIMIT_REACHED blocks new dispatch at the user-level realised daily cap; the agent gate tracks agent daily P/L; accounting withholds daily loss when outcomes are unknown. A breach blocks entries but does not liquidate open positions.
rows.acceptance_criterion: (a) Breach detected from realised + floating P/L including costs within one evaluation cycle; (b) owner-configurable action: block entries, or block and flatten via the gated emergency-close path; (c) measured time from breach to all positions confirmed closed on demo, p95 reported; (d) operator notification on breach.
rows.notes: Entry blocking reaches parity in design; auto-flatten and floating-P/L inclusion are absent.

competitors.approach: Weekly loss auto-liquidation locks the account until the Sunday open; trailing max drawdown in EOD or real-time mode.
MaxDrawdown evaluates any lookback window (lookback_period or candles).

rows.arx_current_state: maxWeeklyLossUsd is stored in agent settings and profiles but is not evaluated by the execution gate or permission evaluator (audit gap G5 still open).
arx_evidence: grep: no weekly reference in executionGate.ts / executionPermission.ts
rows.acceptance_criterion: WEEKLY_LOSS_CAP_REACHED refuses entries when the rolling 7-day realised (and optionally floating) agent loss reaches the cap; unknown accounting refuses; PostgreSQL tests at UTC boundaries.

competitors.approach: StoplossGuard (N stoplosses in lookback → lock, global or per pair), CooldownPeriod (per-pair re-entry lock), LowProfitPairs; supported in backtesting with --enable-protections; /locks and /unlock.

rows.arx_current_state: Quota engine moves agents into RECOVERY/PROTECT regimes that reduce size near loss caps; SYMBOL- and STRATEGY-scoped kill switches exist. No automatic time-boxed per-symbol cooldown lock after a stop-out was found in the reviewed files.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Configurable automatic lock after N losing exits per agent/symbol within a lookback, with audited expiry; included in the agent replay harness so its effect is measured out of sample.

rows.capability: Mandatory protective stop held at the broker

competitors.approach: stoploss_on_exchange places the stop on the exchange after entry fills; on placement failure emergency_exit (default market) exits; re-creates a manually cancelled stop every stoploss_on_exchange_interval (default 60 s).
ATM strategies submit stop and target automatically; server-side ATMs attach them on partial or full fill and cancel the sibling when one fills.
ProtectionType Relative/Absolute SL/TP on orders and positions.

rows.arx_current_state: No thesis or no stop → refusal (NO_THESIS, NO_PROTECTIVE_STOP); Phase B MISSING_STOP_LOSS (admin override exists); SL/TP are sent on the entry request itself; stop changes are recorded only after a settled MODIFY and a matching or stronger observed broker stop.
rows.acceptance_criterion: On demo: 100% of automated entries show a broker-side SL in the position snapshot within one poll; a missing or removed SL is detected and either restored or the position closed within a configured time; admin override use is audited and counted.
rows.notes: No detection/restoration loop for an SL removed after entry was found.

rows.capability: Order size and value limits (fat-finger protection)

competitors.approach: Size Limit, Total Value Limit, Percentage / Number of Ticks away from market, separate algorithm size/value limits; error 383 for size-constraint violations.

rows.arx_current_state: Per-symbol max live lot (Phase B), platform lot ceiling, arming confirmed max lot ≤ 1.0, governor leverage caps, and an anomaly screen that blocks lots far above baseline with fail-safe BLOCK.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Table-driven tests show refusal at limit+1 step for lot, notional and leverage on every automated path (entry, modify, close-by-reverse); audit row names the limit in force.

competitors.approach: None of the researched official docs describe a built-in economic-calendar gate for automated orders.

rows.arx_current_state: News risk is captured at decision time from a hard-coded schedule; it is not re-evaluated before dispatch and there is no live calendar provider (audit gaps G2, G3 still open).
rows.acceptance_criterion: Executor re-reads news risk immediately before draft and refuses on escalation; provider-unavailable state is surfaced; tests for event starting between decision and dispatch.
rows.notes: No competitor baseline; kept because the audit rates it a promotion blocker.

competitors.approach: max_open_trades; only one open trade per pair.

rows.arx_current_state: Checking and reserving capacity happen in one PostgreSQL transaction under the agent lock; pending, dispatched and filled-unclosed entries count; elapsed time never releases capacity.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Under N concurrent cycles (N ≥ 24) no agent exceeds its concurrent or daily cap, including after process restart and UTC rollover; repeated in a deployed staging environment.
rows.notes: Competitor concurrency semantics are not documented, so no 'ahead' claim.

rows.capability: Server-side idempotent order intent and management claims

competitors.approach: Order IDs must increase per client; a reused or lower ID is rejected with error 103 'Duplicate order ID'.
request_id assigned by the terminal links a call to its result, mainly for OrderSendAsync.

rows.arx_current_state: Partial-unique idempotency key per agent; a decision ID is consumed once an execution row commits; draft creation and reservation link are atomic; durable compare-and-set management claims survive restart and are never released by age or timeout.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Zero duplicate broker orders in fault-injection runs (crash after claim, lost response, retry storm) at the server boundary; replicated against a demo broker.
rows.notes: 'Ahead' is limited to documented server-side semantics: IBKR's documented check rejects reused IDs, not logically duplicate intents. Not established end to end (see DUP-2).

competitors.approach: Magic number in each request lets an EA identify and filter its own orders/positions (e.g. after restart).
maintainAndResubmitOrdersOnReconnect resubmits orders attempted while disconnected.

rows.arx_current_state: v131 live deduplication is a RAM ring buffer (lost on restart); v154 duplicate handling does not replay durable original outcomes.
rows.acceptance_criterion: EA persists commandId → outcome durably (file or terminal global variables) before acknowledging; after a forced EA restart mid-command, a redelivered command returns the original outcome and never re-submits; extracted-handler and demo tests.

competitors.approach: MqlTradeRequest.magic is the Expert Advisor ID for grouping its orders.
Trading events fire for both cBot-initiated and manual activity; label semantics not verified in this research.

rows.arx_current_state: v150+ EAs set MagicNumber (v154 default 73154777) and an ARX comment; server attribution (agent, decision, owner) is covered by the command integrity hash/signature.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Every broker deal produced by ARX automation can be attributed to one command and agent from broker history alone (magic + comment/position identifier) in a demo reconciliation report.

competitors.approach: StartBehavior: WaitUntilFlat (default), WaitUntilFlatSynchronizeAccount, ImmediatelySubmit, ImmediatelySubmitSynchronizeAccount, AdoptAccountPosition.
Deployments can be seeded with existing cash and holdings; restarts carry cash, holdings and some open orders.
Open orders are updated on start-up unless exchange.skip_open_order_update is set.

rows.arx_current_state: Agent reconciliation advances executions only from owned command evidence; snapshot ingestion and ghost reconciliation exist. Position uniqueness, ingestion and backfill still key on (user, ticket), and the MT5 position identifier is discarded from the newer EA snapshot.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Account-scoped identity (connection, login, actual server, position identifier); a restart with two accounts holding equal ticket numbers produces zero cross-account matches; documented start-up policy equivalent to wait-until-flat / adopt.

competitors.approach: Restart reloads holdings from the brokerage; algorithm state itself is not saved.

rows.arx_current_state: Lost-command or position mismatch pauses management (no auto-close); unknown evidence and exhausted retries stay HELD; accounting holds block new entries for the affected agent ledger.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Injected mismatches (external close, manual partial close, missing position, extra position) are each detected within one reconciliation cycle and surfaced with an operator action; measured detection lag p95.

rows.capability: Realised P/L reconciled to broker deals and costs

competitors.approach: Deal properties separate profit, commission, swap and fee with position identity (per ARX's prior research).

rows.arx_current_state: Accounting labels RECORDED / INCOMPLETE / UNAVAILABLE and never substitutes zero; broker deal completeness, corrections and costs remain unverified; bound automatic closes record null profit plus a ledger hold.
rows.acceptance_criterion: For a demo period, every closed automated position matches broker deal history on volume, price, commission, swap and fee to the cent; mismatches remain INCOMPLETE with reason.

competitors.approach: Parallel out-of-sample backtest overlaid on each live deployment's equity and fills.

rows.arx_current_state: No equivalent for self-trade agents.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Each agent's live or demo fills are replayed through the same decision logic on the same data, and divergence (entries, exits, P/L) is reported per agent per week.

competitors.approach: Optional automatic restarts are best effort and stop after five failed attempts; state is not saved.
Trade history in an SQL database (separate dry-run database by default).

rows.arx_current_state: Reservations, claims and receipts are durable; a server settlement outbox recovers accepted receipts, but its worker defaults OFF and the migration has not been applied anywhere. A crash between the dispatch claim and mailbox delivery remains an uncertain handoff with no outbox and no audited repair workflow.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Kill -9 at each boundary (after reservation, after claim, after pickup, after broker result, after receipt) recovers to a correct state without duplicate orders; uncertain handoffs are resolved through an audited evidence-based repair action; recovery time measured.

competitors.approach: Terminal transaction queue is bounded (1024) and unordered, so an EA must persist what it needs.

rows.arx_current_state: The settlement outbox is server-side only; results the terminal never delivered are outside its protection.
rows.acceptance_criterion: EA writes each broker result to a durable local outbox before posting and retries until acknowledged; test: network cut after broker fill, EA restart, result still arrives exactly once.

competitors.approach: maintainAndResubmitOrdersOnReconnect; rejectMessagesAboveMaxRate.
TRADE_RETCODE_CONNECTION (10031) when there is no connection to the trade server.

rows.arx_current_state: Phase B blocks dispatch when the EA heartbeat is older than 15 s; heartbeat connection identity is still mutable.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Demo drill: drop EA network for 30 s and 5 min during open positions; no new dispatch while stale, no lost commands, protective commands delivered after reconnect, operator alerted.

competitors.approach: Terminal option disables EA trading when the account is changed (also on profile and symbol/period change).

rows.arx_current_state: Automatic CLOSE/MODIFY re-read login, actual server, mode, ticket, symbol, side and volume immediately before CTrade. Entry routing is not yet pinned to an account/session; a switch between the final check and the broker call is still possible.
rows.arx_evidence_level: C++ harness of extracted MQL; native MetaEditor and broker unverified
rows.acceptance_criterion: Entry and management commands carry a signed target (login, actual server, connection, symbol); terminal refuses on any mismatch; demo drill switches accounts between claim and pickup with zero mis-routed orders.
rows.notes: Management path is closer to parity than entries.

competitors.approach: Algo Trading button disables automated trading for all EAs.
Stop button immediately stops the algorithm; holdings are kept.
/stop stops the trader.

rows.arx_current_state: Platform emergency stop and safety-core kill switch combine in platformStop(), which fails closed on unreadable settings; agent kill switches are checked at the gate and re-checked immediately before submission; release is a single audited operation.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Measured engage → last possible new broker order: zero orders submitted after the engage commit (including commands already in the mailbox); p95 engage latency reported; drill on demo.
rows.notes: Whether already-queued mailbox entry commands are withdrawn on engage was not established in this research.

rows.capability: Pause new entries while still managing exits

competitors.approach: /stopentry stops new trades while exits continue; the pause is not persisted across restart.

rows.arx_current_state: LOCKDOWN/INCIDENT posture pauses autonomous entries; stops refuse only new risk while closes and stop tightening stay open; state is stored in the database.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Pause survives process restart; protective closes and stop tightening succeed during pause in tests and on demo.
rows.notes: 'Ahead' only versus Freqtrade's documented non-persistent pause; broker behaviour unverified.

competitors.approach: Liquidate button sends market orders (market-on-open when closed) then stops the algorithm.
/forceexit all exits every open trade.

rows.arx_current_state: Operator emergency close supports ticket, user, allocation, all-shared and all scopes, only enqueuing closes through the normal gated pipeline; callers require admin/owner, confirmation phrase and reason.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Demo drill with ≥10 positions across ≥2 accounts: time from command to all positions confirmed closed by broker evidence (median/p95), per-ticket outcome, zero closes against the wrong account.

competitors.approach: Per-pair and global locks; /locks and /unlock.

rows.arx_current_state: Kill switch scopes GLOBAL, NEWS, AGENT, STRATEGY, SYMBOL with precedence; per-trader halt and frozen allocations.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Each scope blocks exactly its target and nothing else in a table-driven test; engage/release audited with actor and reason.

rows.capability: Paper / dry-run forward test of automated agents

competitors.approach: dry_run with dry_run_wallet (default 1000) and a separate dry-run database.
Deploy to the Paper Trading brokerage.
Cloud cBots on demo: 1 concurrent instance for 7 days.

rows.arx_current_state: Agents run in SHADOW (audit-only intent, no simulated fill) or LIVE; the executor submits with accountMode 'live' and the instant-trade helper rejects 'paper'. No agent DEMO or paper execution path with fill accounting was found, although the Capital Constitution requires demo execution before real money.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Agent mode DEMO (governed demo queue) and PAPER (real-quote paper book) use the same decision, sizing and gate code as LIVE, with separate ledgers; a 2-week forward run reports fills, slippage and P/L per agent.
rows.notes: Whether per-user SIMULATED routing intercepts agent intents was not established; the executor itself hard-codes live.

rows.capability: Historical replay with realistic ticks, spread and delay

competitors.approach: Every tick based on real ticks; zero/fixed/random execution delay; forward period split (1/2, 1/3, 1/4, custom); genetic optimisation.
Tick data from server; fixed/live/random spread; commission per million.
Broker emulator with intrabar assumptions; bar magnifier uses lower-timeframe bars (up to 200,000).

rows.arx_current_state: Research backtest modules exist, but there is no replay harness for the self-trade agent decision/executor path (audit: 'no backtest harness for live scenario replay'; G4 end-to-end cycle test).
rows.acceptance_criterion: Agent replay on broker tick history with spread, commission and delay models, walk-forward splits, and recorded experiment count; results reproducible from a commit and dataset hash.

competitors.approach: Trade history stored in an SQL database; Telegram /status shows open trades and pending orders.
Alert log shows webhook delivery status; webhooks may occasionally fail to arrive.

rows.arx_current_state: Append-only ledgers by constitution; dispatch claim and its audit commit in one transaction (audit failure rolls back the claim); autonomous cycle aborts if the audit insert fails.
rows.acceptance_criterion: For a sampled set of automated orders, the audit chain reconstructs decision → admission → draft → claim → pickup → broker result → settlement with timestamps and actors, with no gaps.
rows.notes: Competitor audit atomicity is undocumented; no comparison claim.

rows.capability: Mode control and LIVE escalation consent

competitors.approach: readOnlyApi blocks modifications through the API; trusted IPs / localhost-only.
Global Algo Trading toggle; per-EA permissions; WebRequest URL allowlist.

rows.arx_current_state: PAPER/DEMO/LIVE per user; escalation to LIVE requires the exact phrase 'CONFIRM LIVE MODE' and a ≥10-character reason; every change audited; LIVE also requires the server env flag and all Phase B gates.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Truth-table tests for every transition; no automated path can raise authority without an audited owner action.

competitors.approach: Alert thresholds below liquidation thresholds.
Telegram control and status messages.
Staff state no app/email notification when the Daily Loss Limit is hit.

rows.arx_current_state: An OPERATIONAL_RATE_CAP_REACHED monitor exists; reconciliation lag, unresolved-claim age, rejection/duplicate rates and cycle latency SLOs are listed as missing.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Defined SLOs with alert rules for: HELD settlements, unresolved claims older than X, reconciliation lag, EA heartbeat staleness, loss-limit breach, kill-switch engage; alert delivery tested end to end.

competitors.approach: Cloud cBots run with the app closed; up to 10 concurrent live instances (broker-dependent).
Cloud live deployments with optional automatic restart.

rows.arx_current_state: By policy there is no always-on autonomous loop; cycles are admin-triggered. MT5 execution depends on a terminal-side EA.
rows.acceptance_criterion: Owner-approved scheduler with explicit enable, bounded cadence, health checks and automatic disable on SLO breach; demonstrated on demo for 7 days.

competitors.approach: Webhook receiver must respond within 3 s or the request is cancelled; ports 80/443 only.

rows.acceptance_criterion: End-to-end median/p95/p99 from decision commit to broker result receipt on demo, acknowledgement and completion measured separately; receipt p95 ≤ 100 ms locally under the mixed fixture.

competitors.approach: Up to 10 concurrent live cloud instances; 1 on demo.

Broker Integration API lets brokers expose order placement and position closing in TradingView.

rows.arx_current_state: MT5 via terminal-side EA only (constitutionally required when no direct broker API exists).
rows.acceptance_criterion: A second certified venue adapter behind the same Trade Engine contract, passing the same duplicate/recovery/reconciliation suite.

competitors.approach: MQL5 Expert Advisors.
C# cBots with events and async APIs.
Pine Script strategies with alert messages.
Python strategies with protections and hyperopt.

ranked_gaps.title: Truthful terminal fill results
ranked_gaps.why: A broker partial fill (10010) is reported as REJECTED by v154, and v131 reports LIVE_FILLED from the CTrade boolean with the requested lot as executed volume. Real exposure can diverge from ARX's record.
next_steps: Map retcodes exactly per the MQL5 table in both EAs: 10009 FILLED, 10010 PARTIAL, 10008 PLACED, connection/timeout codes UNKNOWN (never REJECTED).
Add ResultVolume, ResultPrice, ResultDeal, request_id and the deal's position identifier (via HistoryDealSelect) to every result payload.
Server: accept PARTIAL with executed volume; never default executed volume to requested volume; UNKNOWN goes to reconciliation.
Extend the extracted C++ handler harness with a retcode matrix; schedule a demo partial-fill/rejection test under owner authorisation.

ranked_gaps.title: Agent DEMO / paper forward testing
ranked_gaps.why: The Capital Constitution requires demo execution before real money, but the agent executor only submits LIVE intents; SHADOW records intents without fills.
next_steps: Add agent modes DEMO and PAPER that reuse decision, sizing, admission and gate code and route to the governed DEMO queue or the real-quote paper book.
Separate agent ledgers per mode; reports must label simulated vs broker-demo fills.
Run a 2-week forward test per profile and publish fills, slippage and P/L (no profitability claims).

ranked_gaps.title: Durable handoff on both sides of the bridge
ranked_gaps.why: Claim-to-mailbox has no outbox, EA deduplication is RAM-only, and terminal results are not durably queued. A crash or restart at these points can lose or repeat a broker action.
next_steps: Server: transactional dispatch outbox written in the claim transaction, delivered idempotently.
EA: persist commandId → outcome before acknowledging; replay original outcome on redelivery; local result outbox retried until acknowledged.
Audited evidence-based repair action for uncertain handoffs (no time-based release).
Kill -9 fault matrix at each boundary in the PostgreSQL + extracted-EA lanes.

ranked_gaps.title: Account-scoped identity and entry account pinning
ranked_gaps.why: Positions key on (user, ticket), the MT5 position identifier is discarded, and entry routing can still pick or rebind a bridge after admission.
next_steps: Implement slice B (signed immutable entry target checked by the terminal before mutation) and slice C (additive identity migration: connection, login, actual server, position identifier) from SELF_TRADING_DISPATCH_AUTHORITY_2026_10_26.md.
Tests: equal ticket numbers on two accounts; account switch between claim and pickup.

ranked_gaps.title: Loss limits: weekly cap and breach response
ranked_gaps.why: maxWeeklyLossUsd is stored but never evaluated; a daily-loss breach blocks entries but does not flatten, and floating P/L is not included.
next_steps: Add WEEKLY_LOSS_CAP_REACHED to the execution permission evaluator using rolling 7-day realised (and optionally floating) P/L; unknown accounting refuses.
Owner-configurable breach action: block, or block and flatten through emergencyClose; notify the operator.
Measure breach-to-flat time on demo.

ranked_gaps.title: Dispatch-time spread and news re-check
ranked_gaps.why: Spread and news risk are judged at decision time only (audit G1, G3).
next_steps: Executor re-reads the live quote and news risk immediately before draft; refuses SPREAD_TOO_WIDE / NEWS_RISK_ESCALATED; unobservable inputs refuse.

ranked_gaps.title: Execution-quality and latency measurement
ranked_gaps.why: No per-fill slippage or end-to-end latency is recorded, so execution quality cannot be compared with anything.
next_steps: Record requested vs fill price, signed slippage and stage timestamps per automated fill; median/p95/p99 dashboards; include in demo reports.

ranked_gaps.title: Margin-aware pre-check
ranked_gaps.why: No OrderCheck() call; agent admission ignores margin.
next_steps: Call OrderCheck() in the EA before entry and report margin projections; add margin-aware agent admission using broker-reported requirements.

ranked_gaps.title: Alerting and SLOs
ranked_gaps.why: Reliability doc lists missing SLOs for reconciliation lag, unresolved claims, rejection/duplicate rates.
next_steps: Define SLOs and alert rules; test delivery end to end.

ranked_gaps.title: Agent replay harness
ranked_gaps.why: No tick-level replay of the agent path with spread, commission and delay.
next_steps: Build replay on broker tick history with walk-forward splits and recorded experiment counts.
